To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) generalization by asking a question can reduce the over-generalization problem, and (2) generalization back-propagates from a confirmed generalization to the precedent rules in a sequence and reduces the number of questions needed by the system.

(a) the parsing process can provide a good source of learning examples, (b) the parsing process and the learning process can interact to utilize acquired parsing-related knowledge to improve parsing, (c) the relaxation parsing mechanism can improve the performance of parsing, and (d) a concept hierarchy can be maintained to help generalization by asking question and to help the relaxation parsing mechanism.
parsing is a problem-solving process, and learning is a generalization of problem-solving heuristics.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following issues: (1) How can parsing be used to drive learning in language acquisition? (2) How can the learning process be integrated with the parsing process? (3) How can parsing-related knowledge be maintained and used?
how a parser can be improved through machine learning.
how parsing and learning can be integrated to improve the performance of parsing.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
parsing and learning can be integrated to achieve natural language acquisition.
the parsing-driven generalization approach can be used to achieve natural language acquisition.
parsing and learning are mutually beneficial to each other, and that the proposed system is able to learn parsing rules and classify lexicons in a way that is consistent with human acquisition.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have successfully integrated parsing and learning in a single system and have demonstrated that parsing-driven generalization can be an effective approach for language acquisition.
the parser and learner are tightly integrated and that the parser is the primary learner and driver for learning.
the parsing-driven approach to language acquisition has a good potential for practical use in natural language processing systems.
The main takeaway from our work is that
parsing can be used to learn parsing-related knowledge.
parsing can be used to drive generalization for natural language acquisition.
parsing and learning can be integrated in an effective way.
